clue.text: Associated work generating income — 1 divided by 3.14159… — during terror

indicators.note: generating is read as producing the parts within the word supplied by the next fodder, which is cut open to hold them

parts.note: income is read as in COME: the word come opened up to take the rest

indicators.note: during says one piece is set within the span of the other

parts.note: terror is sheer panic

indicators.note: a number divided by another is split here, with the second placed in the middle of the first

parts.note: 1 written out as a word is one
3.14159… is the value of the Greek constant pi

explanation.surface: A financial puzzle: something about earnings, with pi arithmetic thrown in, during a reign of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'income' does double duty in the surface: read as 'in come', the word come is the outer shell, opened by 'generating'. 3.14159… is pi.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion piece is a work written to be paired with or complement another, so it is an associated work.

clue.text: Writer, with (hard) luck, far from 1 acrosses

parts.note: chalk is something you write with on a blackboard
with can mean and, joining two things
hard cheese is British slang for bad luck, so cheese alone stands for luck

explanation.surface: A writer down on their luck, far from the works that go with theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD CHEESE is old British slang for bad luck; the bracket lets the setter drop the 'hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things as different as chalk and cheese are utterly unlike, the opposite of matched pairs.

clue.text: Shield bird from car turning up with permit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tram is a tramcar
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: A heraldic bird emerges from a car that has turned up with a permit.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a martlet is a stylised footless bird borne on shields.

clue.text: An omelette with a different base said to be irregular

indicators.note: said to be tells us the result is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.words: An omelette with a different base
parts.note: an omelette with its final letters, its base in a down clue, swapped for a different ending such as -ous gives an omel-ous

explanation.surface: An omelette cooked on some other base is said to be an oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: The base of a down entry is its bottom, so the ending of the omelette is changed before the whole is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anomalous deviates from the norm, so it is irregular.

clue.text: First cooky cooked round piano is disgusting

indicators.note: round means the cooked letters go round the next piece

parts.note: first is I, the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed up like ingredients

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: The first cookie, baked around a piano, turns out to be revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges I and COOKY into ICKYOO, and 'round' wraps that around P.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky-poo is a childish slang word for something nasty or sickly, so disgusting.

clue.text: Jotter, not journalist, seen about father

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the journalist goes round the father

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A jotter, not a journalist, is spotted near father.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a pad of paper for jotting notes on, so it is a jotter.

clue.text: Fifty-fifty on bird losing head — it's a promise

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed below the other piece
losing head means the first letter of the bird goes

parts.note: the kiwi is a flightless New Zealand bird
L is the Roman numeral fifty, so two fifties are two Ls

explanation.surface: Splitting half and half on a beheaded bird is a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I will' is giving one's word, the vow made at a wedding.

clue.text: Cause brain damage with swear word

parts.note: con is Italian and musical shorthand for with, as in con brio
a cuss is a curse or swear word

explanation.surface: Swearing is said to harm the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: To concuss is to injure the brain with a blow, causing temporary damage.

clue.text: Rodsmen with new rod after one's able to enter: they weren't approved by 12

indicators.note: to enter means the following pieces go inside the anglers

parts.note: rodsmen are anglers, people who fish with a rod

indicators.note: after means the rearranged rod comes behind the first piece

parts.note: one's able becomes I can

indicators.note: new signals the letters of rod are reformed

explanation.surface: Fishermen with a new rod try to join a club that the bull of 12 didn't sanction.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1896 Pope Leo XIII's bull Apostolicae Curae declared Anglican ordinations invalid, which is why 12 (the papal bull) never approved them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope Leo XIII's bull Apostolicae Curae declared Anglican ordinations null and void, so these were not approved by a papal bull.

clue.text: Bell with tresses topped and tailed

indicators.note: topped means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: tresses are hair

indicators.note: tailed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: tresses are also locks

explanation.surface: A bell decorated with long hair that has been trimmed at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped and tailed' is shared out: the first synonym loses its top, the second its tail. A diving bell is the sense of 'Bell'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving bell is a chamber sealed by its air pressure, a kind of airlock under water.

clue.text: Abortive excursion presently to Versailles building

indicators.note: abortive means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an excursion is a trip
anon is an old word meaning presently, soon

explanation.surface: A cut-short outing will soon get to Versailles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand and Petit Trianon are palaces in the grounds of Versailles.

clue.text: Disposed of a so-called saint

indicators.note: so-called says we judge the words by how they are called out

parts.note: disposed of means killed, so the phrase is killed a

explanation.surface: Someone got rid of a supposed saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St Kilda is a remote Scottish island group; no saint of that name existed, hence a so-called saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilda appears as a saint only in the place name St Kilda, though the saint is fictional.

clue.text: Page for unfinished scrapbook, in cover, for word from Rome

indicators.note: in means the page and scrapbook go inside the cover

parts.note: a pall is a cloth cover, as over a coffin

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut

parts.note: an album is a book for keeping scraps or photos

explanation.surface: A page from an unfinished scrapbook goes inside its cover, ready for a message from Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal bull is a formal decree issued by the Pope, literally a word from Rome.

clue.text: Bad do soon got worse

indicators.note: worse means the letters are put in a damaged, different order

explanation.surface: A bad party soon took a turn for the worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Not so good is a mild idiom for poor or bad.

clue.text: Degree (yes, really!) underlying

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
sic is Latin for thus, used to say a quoted word really was written so

explanation.surface: A degree, honestly, lies at the bottom of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic is fundamental, the foundation underlying everything else.

clue.text: Ablution in Germany and China is a game

parts.note: Bad is German for bath, a wash or ablution
Minton is a famous English make of fine china

explanation.surface: Washing in Germany and China is a sporting pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country beside Germany; it is porcelain, Minton ware from Stoke-on-Trent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a net.

clue.text: Carpenter with salt and vinegar?

definitions.meaning: ... is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter, from wood ...
fried potato strips are what you sprinkle salt and vinegar on in a British chip shop

explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips with salt and vinegar is the classic British takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is both the sailors' nickname for a carpenter and fried potato pieces seasoned with salt and vinegar.

clue.text: Establish ID in monkey, right in time

parts.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp
taken as written

explanation.surface: Identifying a monkey properly, right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Imprinting is how a young animal fixes the identity of its parent.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprint, in animal behaviour, is to fix firmly in the mind who a mother is, establishing identity.

clue.text: Come and dance, keeping company with the devil

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
dance means the letters move about into a new pattern

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and dance in company with Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like part of the definition, but it is only a link; 'dance' works on the letters of 'Come and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cacodemon is an evil spirit, a malignant demon, so a devil.

clue.text: Wreath for little fellow?

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
-let is a diminutive ending, as in piglet, so it means little

explanation.surface: A garland suitable for a small boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or wreath worn on the head.

clue.text: Spaniard caught — no thanks to legendaryrunner

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: no thanks to means the word for thanks is removed

parts.note: Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek legend, beaten in a footrace by golden apples

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is caught, no thanks to a mythical sprinter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no thanks to' removes TA, British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catalan is a person from Catalonia, a region of Spain.

clue.text: Dictatorship of the proletariat, in a little while caramelised

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a little while
brûlé is French for burnt, used of a caramelised topping as in crème brûlée

explanation.surface: Workers' rule arrives shortly, caramelised like a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob rule is rule by the masses, a sardonic version of the Marxist ideal of workers in power.

clue.text: Cough mixture missing or with child

indicators.note: missing means the following word is taken out

parts.note: an expectorant is a cough medicine

explanation.surface: Short of cough medicine, or pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant woman is pregnant, which is to say with child.

clue.text: Number part of Greek letter? That's funny

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number

indicators.note: part of means only some of the letter's name is used

parts.note: omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A number that is part of a Greek letter strikes you as amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means funny, so it can stand for the exclamation that something is comical.

clue.text: Wood doesn't start in deserted village

indicators.note: doesn't start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: timber is wood

explanation.surface: Wood is not beginning to grow in an abandoned village.
explanation.walkthrough: Imber is a village on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, emptied by the army in 1943 and still uninhabited.
explanation.definitionFit: Imber is the famous English village evacuated for military training and never resettled.

clue.text: Melissa's form is tremendous

indicators.note: form tells us to shape the letters into something new

parts.note: the name Melissa, its possessive ending giving no letter

explanation.surface: Melissa's figure is stunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismal means of earthquakes, earth-shaking, so tremendous in a playful sense.

clue.text: Allow unions to start eating salad

parts.note: to allow is to let
the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of unions

indicators.note: to start picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Permit the unions to begin eating salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is the leafy vegetable that forms the base of a salad.

clue.text: Early terminus for early punishment including two false notes

indicators.note: including means the punishment holds the other letters inside

parts.note: the stocks were a wooden frame for punishing offenders, long out of use

indicators.note: false means the letters are not in their true order
two means the note is taken twice

parts.note: a note, one of the notes, is the word written out

explanation.surface: The end of an early line, where offenders were once punished with two fake banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges the doubled note into TONONTEE. The Stockton and Darlington, opened in 1825, was the first public steam railway; Stockton-on-Tees is in northeast England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees was one end of the Stockton and Darlington Railway of 1825, a terminus of the earliest public line.
